title: A copy of a component is configured, not authored
goal: Selecting a copy of a component shows the same wall of authoring controls the original does: the name, whether it is shared across documents, the list of versions, the list of adjustable things and how to add one. A copy cannot do any of that. What a copy needs is small: which version it shows, and the values of the things the original made adjustable. Show that, and stop showing the rest.
notes:
CORRECTED 2026-09-15 by the runner that claimed this, after reproducing it. The premise below is inverted. A COPY's panel is already configured-not-authored: name as a label, one sentence, a Properties list led by the look picker, a value row per exposed property, and Edit Original / Detach. No name field, no sharing switch, no Add, no minus buttons. What the user clicked was the ORIGINAL, because the FIRST drag of any component off the shelf lands the original and every drag after it lands a copy (StarterComponents.swift:685; reproduced by test run). Acceptance items 1, 2, 4, 5 and 7 are already met in source. Items 3, 6 and 8 need the running app and the Mac's screen has been locked all afternoon, so no walk can run. A decision is open asking what a drag should hand you; this task waits on the answer.

---

Reported by the user on 2026-09-15 with a screenshot of the Component section: 'the component ui for component instances . super confusing. info overload, can't adjust specific component properties defined for it, select a variant...'

The screenshot is the ORIGINAL's panel - it says 'This is the original. Copies you place will follow it.' - and it carries Name, the sharing switch, Versions with Add, and Adjustable with Add and a Label row. That is all authoring. The user's complaint is that selecting a copy does not give them the two things a copy is for: pick a version, set the values.

The app already knows the difference and already says so visually: ComponentPanel.swift:66 has an isInstance flag, four diamonds for an original and one for a copy, with different help text. So the distinction exists in the chrome and not in the contents.

It has also been thought about before, which is worth reading rather than rediscovering: 'a-copy-is-not-asked-to-decide-things-only-its-original-can' is done, as are 'the-knobs-panel-speaks-for-several-copies-at-once' and 'a-copy-does-not-say-which-version-it-is-showing'. Find out what each actually did before changing anything, because the gap the user hit may be narrower than the whole panel - it may be that the version picker is missing from the copy rather than that the copy shows too much.

The principle to land: an original is AUTHORED and a copy is CONFIGURED. Those are two jobs and they should not look the same.

THIS IS MEASURED, NOT JUST FELT. The study 'work-out-whether-the-right-hand-pane-is-carrying' (done, 2026-09-15) measured the dock in the running app: 1052 points of sections against a 968 point viewport at 1680x1000, and Position & Size never wholly on screen at any window size. Its page is docs/design/mocks/pages/pane-load.html and its audit is queue/audits/2026-09-15-pane-load.json. Read both before starting: the measuring is done and should not be redone.

The four threads are filed as four tasks because they are four different fixes, but they are one complaint and whoever picks one up should read the others.

THE MODEL, corrected by the user on 2026-09-15 while walking away. First: "I don't think 'Variants' is any better. component properties makes sense. Variant is a property of the component." Then, still thinking: "Maybe State is a separate property. or maybe variant is hierarchical."

So the direction is ONE concept, not two sections. A component has PROPERTIES. What the panel currently splits into 'Adjustable' and 'Versions' is one list: a property is anything a copy can be given its own answer for, and one KIND of property is a set of named looks, which is what Versions is today. That is why neither name worked: they are two names for halves of one idea.

This also collapses the copy's panel into the same list with values in it instead of definitions, which is what the sibling task a-copy-of-a-component-is-configured-not-authored is for.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN, and the user was explicitly unsure, so settle it with a prototype rather than a preference:
- Is a state just one property among many, named State with the values rest, hovered, pressed and disabled? That is the simplest answer and probably right.
- Or does a component need more than one look-changing property at once, so that a Button has a Type of primary or secondary AND a State of rest or hovered, and the two combine into a matrix of drawings? That is what the user means by variant being hierarchical, and it is what real button components need almost immediately.
The second is strictly more powerful and strictly more work, and the first is a special case of it. Prototype the matrix case before choosing, because designing for one look-changing property and discovering later that two are needed is a rewrite rather than an addition.

Do NOT settle this by picking a word. The question is whether the model holds one named-set property or several, and the naming falls out of the answer.
acceptance: Selecting a copy shows what a copy can actually change: which version it is showing, and a value for each adjustable thing the original defined
Authoring controls are not shown on a copy: naming the component, sharing it across documents, adding or removing versions, and adding or removing adjustable things all belong to the original
Picking which version a copy shows is obvious and quick, because that is the main thing somebody selects a copy to do
The way back to the original is one clear move, since that is where the hidden controls live
With several copies picked it still reads as one panel rather than repeating itself, which the existing behaviour already gets right and must not lose
The panel is measurably shorter for a copy than for an original: give both heights in points
An original still shows everything it shows today, unchanged
Audit under queue/audits/ with the panel captured for an original and for a copy side by side, and anything rough filed as a follow-up

REPRODUCED, and the premise turns out to be inverted. A COPY's panel is already configured-not-authored: InspectorPanel.swift:837 routes a picked copy to ComponentInstanceInspector, which shows the component's name as a label (not a field), one sentence, a Properties list whose top row is the variant picker wearing the author's own word, a value row per property the original exposed, and Edit Original / Detach. There is no Name field, no Share across documents switch, no Add, no version list, no minus buttons. The original's ComponentInspector (line 182) is the only thing that carries those.

THE REAL CAUSE, reproduced by running the model rather than reading it. The FIRST time you drag a component off the Library shelf you get the ORIGINAL, not a copy; every drag after that gives a copy. StarterComponents.swift:685 - insertStarterComponent returns insertComponentInstance only when a main already exists, otherwise it adds the main itself. Test run (Tests/PhotonzCoreTests, scratch suite, Scripts/test.sh --filter FirstDropIsTheOriginalRepro): 'REPRO first isMainComponent=true isCopy=false / REPRO second isMainComponent=false isCopy=true', 1 test passed. Existing coverage says the same in StarterComponentTests.swift:172 droppingTheSameStarterTwiceMakesACopy.

So the user dragged one Button on, clicked it, and got the authoring wall because that Button WAS the original. Their screenshot proves it: the sentence on it reads 'This is the original. Copies you place will follow it.', which ComponentPanel.swift:257 only prints when the copy count is zero - one drag, no copies. The panel was not lying to them; the app handed them the wrong thing to click. That is why every acceptance item about the copy's panel already passes in source: 1, 2, 4, 5 and 7 are met today by the three sibling tasks named in the notes plus this morning's Properties rename.

Adversarial review of the copy's panel, walking it as a first-time user. What it offers is right and short. What is left rough and did NOT earn a task: (a) the Layout section on a copy prints the ORIGINAL's arrangement as eight dead grey rows (Arrangement, Smallest height, Padding, the room sentence, Horizontal, Vertical, plus a reason line) - that is the last block of the original's business shown on a copy, but a-copy-is-not-asked-to-decide-things-only-its-original-can deliberately chose read-only rows over hiding ('a copy with none reads as a bug'), and the panel-sections feature that landed this morning already lets the user switch the whole Layout section off, so reversing it now would be re-litigating a settled call without the user. (b) ComponentInstanceInspector's 'Make <name> a Property' press and ComponentPieceInspector's 'Make Its Wording a Property' are authoring acts on a copy, which acceptance item 2 forbids on a literal reading - kept deliberately: they appear only as the way out of an edit the app just refused, and they act on the original.
